chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Returning the oboe, and the Lorais oboe he later sold
summary: He gave back Dr. Holmes's oboe, got a brand-new Lorais from the school, later bought one himself in New York, and sold it in the Depression for twenty-five dollars.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Once you got the saxophone, I guess you gave the oboe back to Dr. Holmes?
Oh, no. I gave him his oboe back before I went in high school. After the year was up and he told me after doing so good on the oboe, he decided to keep me on it, then I gave it back to him.

But when I went to high school, they heard that I played oboe and they needed oboe players in the school orchestra. And I told them I didn't have an oboe. I said, "I don't mind practicing with the band and one thing or another, but I don't have one." "That's no problem. You just go to this address here, and they'll have an instrument for you."

So okay, I went and I got the instrument. It was a Lorais(?) oboe, brand-new. That's just like somebody gives you a car, and they come up and give you a Rolls-Royce. You know? It was about the best of the oboes; the Lorais(?)
was the best. And brand-new. And I couldn't believe it. So I played it. I was glad to play it, you know. Oh, it was beautiful.
And that was the instrument that you played in the Boston Symphony with?
Yeah. Yeah, it was a beautiful instrument.
You never thought of later on buying an oboe for yourself?
I did buy one later on.

I bought a Lorais(?) oboe later on. I kept it... That's after I came to New York. And I kept it and kept it, and I never played it, and the thing was just deteriorating in the case. And I finally sold it during the Depression for twenty-five dollars. Not that I needed the money. I was just tired of seeing it sitting around. I sold it for twenty-five dollars. It was worth about two-hundred and fifty then. And now, I don't know what... I guess you can buy a home cheaper than you can buy an oboe. They're very expensive things. Well, with this inflation and everything, you know...
